question: Few renowned artists of ________ dance style in India are Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and Kumudini Lakhia.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathak:**

 
 
• Kathak is a major classical dance form originating from northern India.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, rapid spins (chakkars), and expressive gestures.
 
• The word "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "katha," meaning "story," and story-telling is a key element of the dance.
 
• Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao, and Kumudini Lakhia are indeed renowned exponents of Kathak, contributing significantly to its evolution and popularization.
 
• Kathak has strong Hindu and Muslim influences, and has evolved through both temple and court traditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhau:**

 
 
• Chhau is a semi-classical dance form with martial, tribal, and folk traditions.
 
• It originates from the eastern Indian states of Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal.
 
• Chhau dances are characterized by vigorous movements, acrobatic leaps, and the use of masks in some styles.
 
• The dance often depicts episodes from epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana, as well as local legends.
 
• There are three main styles of Chhau, named after the location where they are performed: Purulia Chhau, Seraikella Chhau, and Mayurbhanj Chhau.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri:**
 
 
• Manipuri is a classical dance form originating from the northeastern Indian state of Manipur.
 
• It is known for its graceful and fluid movements, particularly the raslila, which depicts the love story of Radha and Krishna.
 
• Manipuri dance uses distinctive cylindrical skirts (called 'kumil') and veils.
 
• The dance emphasizes gentle swaying movements and subtle hand gestures.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the Vaishnavism tradition.
 
 
 
• **Odissi:**
 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form originating from the eastern Indian state of Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by its tribhangi (three-bend) posture, graceful movements, and expressive facial expressions.
 
• Odissi dance is deeply rooted in the temple traditions of Odisha, and many of its movements are inspired by sculptures found in ancient temples.
 
• The dance involves expressions of divine and human love.
 
• Odissi was reconstructed in the mid 20th century, after a period of decline.
